Validate a bounded caster attack or contact-breaking alternative under guard-pull pressure before changing priorities. review.review: The run ended with a living, fully healed hero because entrance-shop searching exhausted its budget, not because the game clock stopped. At decision 1651 (line 4829), both entrance branches were observed. After checking door 764 at decision 1654 (lines 4835–4836), decision 1655 (lines 4837–4838) pursued a deeper frontier while original door 395 remained unchecked. The shop selector merged every checked-door branch into one component and always preferred its frontiers, letting deeper chambers consume all 80 shop inputs. Decisions 1892–1894 (lines 5447–5452) show the final approach, last usable healing, and planner exhaustion at 50/50 HP. The proposed correction searches shallower observed entrance branches before deeper ones, using the same admitted paths and unchanged budget. A limited helper-state reconstruction matches the original actions and reasons for decisions 1651–1655; candidate copies first differ at 1655 and consume no later observations. This is not a reconstruction of all runtime memory or proof that the shop would be reached. The new deterministic regression fails on the original selector and passes on the candidate. The full unittest report is green: 1,614 tests, four skipped. The surrounding shell subsequently returned a termination status, so a clean shell-wrapper exit is not established.
review.learnings: Do not let one checked entrance exit turn shop scouting into a deep floor sweep while another observed entrance branch remains unchecked. Preserve safety admission, mandatory progression pickups, honest visit receipts and the planner-exhaustion outcome; choosing a better ordered approach does not establish shop discovery or puzzle completion.
